# CLI reference

<!-- Generated by `go run ./hack/gendocs`; do not edit. -->

Every command also accepts the global flags `--config` (config file, default `$ICARO_CONFIG` or `~/.icaro/config/icaro.yaml`) and `--home` (state root, default `$ICARO_HOME` or `~/.icaro`).

## `icaro claude`

Run claude in an isolated session for the current repository

```text
icaro claude [ARGS...]
```

## `icaro codex`

Run codex in an isolated session for the current repository

```text
icaro codex [ARGS...]
```

## `icaro config`

Inspect configuration

Subcommands: `show`

## `icaro config show`

Print the effective configuration as YAML (token redacted)

```text
icaro config show
```

## `icaro credential`

Manage host-bound integration credentials

Aliases: credentials

Subcommands: `add` `list` `remove`

## `icaro credential add`

Store `<integration>.<name>` in the daemon's secret store. The value is read from stdin.
Action credentials are bound to the manifest's hosts (plus a configured base_url host)
unless --host is given; the executor refuses to send them anywhere else. Webhook
secrets (webhook_secret) are only used to verify inbound requests and get no binding.

```text
icaro credential add INTEGRATION [NAME] [flags]
```

```text
      --host strings   bind to these hosts instead of the manifest's (repeatable; *.domain allowed)
      --yes            store without asking to confirm the binding
```

## `icaro credential list`

List integration credentials (names and host bindings, never values)

```text
icaro credential list
```

## `icaro credential remove`

Delete a credential (requires --yes)

```text
icaro credential remove NAME [flags]
```

```text
      --yes   confirm deletion
```

## `icaro login`

Log the profile's agent in once; the login seeds every session of the profile


## `icaro mcp`

Bridges an MCP client speaking stdio to Ícaro's MCP server.

On the host (no --socket) it connects to the daemon's /mcp endpoint, scoped to the project of --project
(default: the current directory's git repository). Inside a session container the agent config runs
`icaro mcp --socket /icaro/mcp.sock`, whose scope is fixed by the session.

```text
icaro mcp [flags]
```

```text
      --agent string     agent name recorded on memories
      --project string   project directory that scopes memory (default: current git repository)
      --socket string    session MCP socket (inside agent containers: /icaro/mcp.sock)
```

## `icaro memory`

Shared memory holds decisions, tasks, findings and handoffs plus indexed files, symbols, ADRs and commits.
MCP-capable agents use it through `icaro mcp`; these commands are the HTTP/CLI fallback. See docs/memory.md.

```text
      --json                print JSON
      --project string      project directory (its git repository defines the project) (default ".")
      --project-id string   project id (overrides --project)
```

Subcommands: `handoff` `import` `ingest` `project` `query` `show` `write`

## `icaro memory query`

Search memory (newest first when TEXT is empty)

```text

```

```text
      --agent string    filter by agent
      --branch string   this branch plus project-wide memories
      --kind strings    filter by kind (repeatable)
      --limit int       maximum results (default 10)
      --since string    only newer than a duration (24h) or RFC 3339 time
      --source string   source prefix (e.g. internal/api/)
      --status string   handoff status: pending | accepted
```

## `icaro memory show`


## `icaro memory write`

Record a decision, task, finding or handoff

```text
icaro memory write --kind KIND --title TITLE [flags]
```

```text
      --agent string        agent name to record
      --body string         details
      --body-file string    read the body from a file (- for stdin)
      --kind string         decision | task | finding | handoff
      --source string       path, URL or commit this comes from
      --supersedes string   id of a memory this replaces
      --title string        short title
      --ttl duration        expire after this duration (e.g. 72h)
```

## `icaro preview`

Per-worktree previews: compose projects routed at a predictable URL

```text
      --json   print JSON
```

Subcommands: `allow` `down` `lint` `list` `logs` `rm` `up`

## `icaro preview allow`

Allowing a finding weakens the preview's isolation from your machine (e.g. a privileged container or a host mount). The override is recorded per worktree and finding.

```text
icaro preview allow PATH --finding ID [--finding ID...] --yes [flags]
```

```text
      --finding stringArray   finding ID to allow (repeatable)
      --yes                   confirm the override
```

## `icaro preview down`

```text
icaro preview down [PATH]
```


## `icaro preview list`

```text
icaro preview list
```

## `icaro preview logs`

Show the compose logs of a preview

```text

```

```text
      --tail int   lines per container (default 200)
```

## `icaro preview rm`

Tear a preview down and remove its containers, volumes and record

```text

```

```text
      --yes   confirm the removal
```

## `icaro preview up`

Bring up the preview of a worktree (default: current directory)


```text
      --force   restart even if the configuration did not change
```

## `icaro run`

Start a workflow run manually. The run's ${{ trigger.* }} payload comes
from --trigger-json/--trigger-file and --set key=value; any field the
workflow requires that is still missing is prompted for on a terminal.

```text
icaro run NAME [flags]
```

```text
      --json                  print JSON
      --no-prompt             fail instead of prompting for missing trigger fields
      --set stringArray       trigger field key=value (repeatable; numbers/booleans/JSON are parsed)
      --trigger-file string   trigger payload from a JSON file (- for stdin)
      --trigger-json string   trigger payload as a JSON object
      --wait                  stream logs and wait for the run to finish (exit 1 unless it succeeds)
```

## `icaro serve`

Run the daemon (one per user; Unix socket, optional TCP with --listen)

```text
icaro serve [flags]
```

```text
      --allow-remote       let --listen bind a non-loopback address (plain HTTP; prefer a TLS reverse proxy to 127.0.0.1)
      --background         start the daemon detached and return once it answers
      --listen string      also listen on TCP (e.g. 127.0.0.1:8787); every TCP request needs an API token
      --log-level string   debug | info | warn | error (default "info")
      --pprof              serve /debug/pprof on the Unix socket only (also daemon.pprof)
```

## `icaro setup`

setup is idempotent: it shows a diff of every change and asks before applying it.
Running it again changes nothing unless something is missing or you pass --update-images.

```text
icaro setup [flags]
```

```text
      --skip-images     do not pull or pin profile images
      --update-images   pull the latest images and re-pin their digests
      --yes             apply changes without asking (non-interactive)
```

## `icaro update`

Downloads the release archive, checksums.txt and its ed25519 signature,
verifies both, smoke-tests the new binary, swaps it in atomically and keeps
the previous binary for --rollback. Config and the database under ~/.icaro are
never touched; a running daemon is restarted and re-attaches its sessions.

```text
icaro update [flags]
```

```text
      --check            only report whether an update is available
      --no-restart       do not restart a running daemon
      --rollback         restore the binary kept by the last update
      --version string   install this version instead of the latest (e.g. v0.3.0)
      --yes              confirm replacing the installed binary
```

## `icaro usage`

Parses the Claude Code transcripts in every profile home (and, with
--host-claude, your own ~/.claude, read-only) into per-day, per-model token
counts. Each row names its source and confidence; rows whose transcript is
gone come from saved snapshots (confidence "snapshot"). Costs come from a list-price
table and are always estimates; unpriced models show no cost. Alerts fire when
a day's estimated spend reaches usage.daily_limit_usd, in usage.timezone.

```text
icaro usage [flags]
```

```text
      --host-claude    also read your own ~/.claude transcripts (read-only)
      --json           print JSON
      --no-save        do not store snapshots in the database
      --since string   window start: a duration in days (7d) or a date (2025-03-01) (default "7d")
```
